title: Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide)
name: Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide)
description: Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide). Chemistry: Zn anode, MnO2 cathode, KOH electrolyte. Nominal voltage 1.5 V, specific energy ~100 Wh/kg, single use (primary). Typical uses: AA/AAA/C/D household cells, remotes, toys, flashlights. The workhorse disposable cell of the modern household; long shelf life and leak-resistant builds made it the default primary battery worldwide.
how_it_works: A battery converts chemical energy to electrical energy through redox reactions: oxidation at the anode releases electrons, reduction at the cathode consumes them, and the electrolyte carries ions between the electrodes to complete the circuit.
key_points: Chemistry: Zn anode, MnO2 cathode, KOH electrolyte
Typical uses: AA/AAA/C/D household cells, remotes, toys, flashlights

demo.program:
# Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide) -- energy demo
voltage = 1.5  # nominal volts
capacity_ah = 2.5  # typical capacity, Ah
energy_wh = voltage * capacity_ah
mass_kg = energy_wh / 100  # from specific energy
print("Cell: Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide)")
print("Energy: %.2f Wh, about %.3f kg of cells per 100 Wh" % (energy_wh, 100 * mass_kg / energy_wh))
demo.note: Compute the stored energy of a typical Alkaline (Zinc-Manganese Dioxide) cell.

chemistry: Zn anode, MnO2 cathode, KOH electrolyte
typical_uses: AA/AAA/C/D household cells, remotes, toys, flashlights
requirements: Match voltage and current to the device; observe polarity; store in cool dry conditions.
citations: IEC battery standards series; US DOE energy storage handbooks
